title: Finder wave FINAL REPLY
description: Schema every finder lane's FINAL REPLY is validated against (ADR-018 §1). Finders emit only the fp-input fields (wave, severity, files, claim, evidence); id/status/round/lane/ts are assigned by ff-findings.sh append and never come from a lane, since ts especially must never enter a packet (ADR-012 cache-key purity).

findings.description: May be empty - a clean sweep is a valid, reportable result, not an error.

wave.description: Catalogue wave name that produced this finding (e.g. "qa", "security", "a11y") - the first component of the fp fingerprint.

severity.description: critical = data loss, auth bypass, crash on main path. high = wrong results, injection, broken feature. medium = degraded UX, missing validation, perf cliff. low = polish, naming, minor inconsistency.

files.description: Repo-relative paths touched by the finding. Sorted and joined into the fp fingerprint at append time - the lane does not need to sort them.

claim.description: One-sentence defect statement. Lowercased and whitespace-collapsed into the fp fingerprint, so wording drift across otherwise-identical re-runs still dedupes.

evidence.description: Repro steps or observed-vs-expected. NOT part of the fp - evidence may be re-worded across rounds without minting a new finding.

meta.description: No-silent-caps clause: a finder that had to sample, skip a check (e.g. no Playwright available), or otherwise narrow its coverage says so here rather than reporting a clean sweep that wasn't one.

sampled.description: true if this lane did not exhaustively cover its scope (time-boxed, sampled a subset, a tool was unavailable and it fell back to heuristics, etc.).

notes.description: Free text: what was skipped/sampled and why, or empty string when sampled is false.
